epics.summary: Smoke stack to green: fix the defects a live run of deploy/compose.yaml found after dispatch

stories.summary: Give the server image its persona directory, its venv path and a git identity
stories.description: A live run of the compose stack on 2026-10-29 (master 2a667f7) failed three times inside the pipeline container, each on an image fact: personas not found, the dispatch interpreter missing, and git refusing to commit without an identity.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master c57a596 - stand-in of SG-01..SG-06 together: 19003 passed / 3 failed / 42 skipped; none of the 3 failures is in a file this story touches (0 conflicts for SG-01). The image change itself was verified live: with exactly these three edits the pipeline container got past all three failures below.

ROOT CAUSES (verified in a running container, not guessed):
1. deploy/Dockerfile copies personas to /app/agents (`COPY --chown=10001:10001 agents ./agents`) but never sets AGENTS_DIR, so pipeline/paths.py falls back to `~/.claude/agents` = /var/lib/pipeline/.claude/agents. dispatch_story then fails with `FileNotFoundError: No persona named software-engineer at /var/lib/pipeline/.claude/agents/software-engineer.md`.
2. app/backend_ollama.py sets `_VENV_PYTHON = <repo>/.venv/bin/python3`; the image's virtualenv is /opt/venv, so dispatch fails with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/.venv/bin/python3'`.
3. The image has no git identity; the WIP checkpoint commit fails with `Author identity unknown`.

MAKE EXACTLY THESE EDITS to deploy/Dockerfile (anchored, not by line number):
- In the runtime-stage `ENV` block, immediately after the line `    WORKTREE_ROOT=/var/lib/pipeline/worktrees \`, insert these five lines:
    AGENTS_DIR=/app/agents \
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=pipeline \
    GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=pipeline@localhost \
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=pipeline \
    GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=pipeline@localhost \
- In the `RUN chmod 0755 ./deploy/entrypoint.sh \` instruction, insert ` && ln -s /opt/venv /app/.venv \` as the line immediately after it.
The git identity is a default an operator overrides with the same variables at `docker run -e`/compose `environment:`; say so in deploy/README.md.

DOCS: in deploy/README.md's `## Required environment` table add three rows (AGENTS_DIR default `/app/agents`; GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME default `pipeline`; GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL default `pipeline@localhost`, with one sentence that commits the server makes carry this identity and an operator should set it). Add one sentence under `## Volumes` that /app/.venv is a symlink to /opt/venv because the local dispatch harness launches `<repo>/.venv/bin/python3`.

TESTS (write first, watch them fail, new file tests/unit/test_deploy_image_runtime_env.py, read deploy/Dockerfile as text like tests/unit/test_deploy_dockerfile.py does):
- the runtime stage sets AGENTS_DIR=/app/agents, and that path is where `COPY ... agents ./agents` lands under WORKDIR /app;
- the runtime stage sets all four GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* variables to non-empty values;
- the runtime stage creates the symlink `/app/.venv` -> `/opt/venv`;
- negative: none of the new ENV values contains a secret-looking key (no TOKEN/KEY/SECRET/PASSWORD in the variable names you added);
- negative: the builder stage does not set AGENTS_DIR (assert it only appears after the final FROM).
Assert membership/ordering only, never the full ENV block text.

SUCCESS: the five tests pass; `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` and `ruff check .` are green. Do not modify any existing test.

stories.summary: Make the local agent call the provider the harness named, not the PIPELINE_LOCAL_PROVIDER default
stories.description: The dispatched local agent ignores LOCAL_AGENT_PROVIDER for its chat turns and resolves the provider from PIPELINE_LOCAL_PROVIDER (default ollama), so a role pinned to lmstudio or mlx talks the Ollama wire protocol.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master c57a596 - stand-in of SG-01..SG-06: this story's stand-in broke exactly 2 pre-existing tests, both pre-authorized below; 0 other conflicts.

ROOT CAUSE (verified live 2026-10-29): app/harness.py passes the resolved provider to the agent subprocess as LOCAL_AGENT_PROVIDER, and scripts/local_agent_config.py reads it into PROVIDER. But the chat turn for a non-Ollama provider calls `origin["inference_providers"].get_local_provider().chat(...)` with NO name, and app/inference_providers.get_local_provider(name=None) then resolves from PIPELINE_LOCAL_PROVIDER (default "ollama"). Observed: agent.log `[boot] ... provider=lmstudio` followed by `LLM call failed: Client error '404 Not Found' for url 'http://model:8080/api/chat'` (the Ollama path on an OpenAI-compatible server).

FIX (two identical one-line edits, anchored):
- scripts/local_agent_chat.py, in `_provider_chat_turn_impl`: replace `origin["inference_providers"].get_local_provider().chat(` with `origin["inference_providers"].get_local_provider(origin["PROVIDER"]).chat(`.
- scripts/local_agent_oracle_chat.py, in its `_provider_chat_turn_impl`: the same replacement.
Nothing else changes; do not touch the Ollama streaming path.

AUTHORIZED EDITS to existing tests (make exactly these two, nothing else; justify them in the commit body as: "the fakes took no argument; the agent now passes the provider name it was launched with"):
- tests/unit/test_local_agent_streaming_and_provider.py line containing `monkeypatch.setattr(la.inference_providers, "get_local_provider", lambda: _FakeProvider())` -> `monkeypatch.setattr(la.inference_providers, "get_local_provider", lambda name=None: _FakeProvider())`
- tests/unit/test_local_agent_oracle_view_and_tamper.py line containing `monkeypatch.setattr(lao.inference_providers, "get_local_provider", lambda: _FakeProvider())` -> `monkeypatch.setattr(lao.inference_providers, "get_local_provider", lambda name=None: _FakeProvider())`

TESTS (write first, new file tests/unit/test_local_agent_provider_name.py; mock only get_local_provider, the external boundary):
- with PROVIDER="lmstudio" and PIPELINE_LOCAL_PROVIDER unset, local_agent's `_provider_chat_turn` calls get_local_provider with "lmstudio";
- with PROVIDER="mlx" and PIPELINE_LOCAL_PROVIDER="ollama" set in the environment, it still calls get_local_provider with "mlx" (the harness value wins);
- the same two cases for local_agent_oracle's `_provider_chat_turn`;
- negative: with PROVIDER="ollama" the chat() wrapper uses the streaming path and never calls get_local_provider (record calls on the fake).

SUCCESS: new tests pass; the two edited tests pass; full suite and `ruff check .` green.

stories.summary: Stop rewriting a registry-declared model tag to the local default model
stories.description: _resolve_local_model treats any model without ':' or '/' as a tier name, so a registry tag like scripted-dispatch (or a bare LM Studio/MLX model id) silently becomes PIPELINE_LOCAL_MODEL_DEFAULT.

stories.summary: Answer the model-list probes in the scripted model server
stories.description: LMStudioProvider probes GET /v1/models (reachable) and GET /api/v0/models (loaded_models); the scripted server 404s both, so the stack reports its only model backend as down.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master c57a596 - stand-in of SG-01..SG-06: 0 conflicts for this story; tests/smoke/test_scripted_model_server.py stayed green with GET answered.

ROOT CAUSE (verified live 2026-10-29): app/inference_providers.py LMStudioProvider.reachable() does `GET {endpoint}/v1/models` and loaded_models() does `GET {endpoint}/api/v0/models`. tests/smoke/scripted_model_server.py `_dispatch` checks `path not in _ACCEPTED_PATHS` BEFORE the method, so both GETs get `404 unknown endpoint` (the model container logged a stream of `scripted model error action=chat.completions status=404`). A probe that reads 'unreachable' can withhold dispatch or review.

FIX (tests/smoke/scripted_model_server.py only):
- Add a module constant `MODEL_LIST_PATHS = frozenset({"/v1/models", "/api/v0/models"})` next to `_ACCEPTED_PATHS`.
- In `_dispatch`, before the `_ACCEPTED_PATHS` check: when `method == "GET"` and the path is in MODEL_LIST_PATHS, reply 200 with `{"object": "list", "data": [...]}` holding one entry per role in ROLE_NAMES: `{"id": "scripted-<role>", "object": "model", "state": "loaded"}`. Use the existing `_send_json`.
- A GET to a model-list path must NOT advance any role cursor (cursor_state() unchanged).
- Every other GET keeps today's behaviour (404 for an unknown path, 405 for GET on the chat path).

TESTS (write first, new file tests/smoke/test_scripted_model_list.py, start the server in-process on port 0 like test_scripted_model_server.py does):
- GET /v1/models returns 200 and lists scripted-dispatch, scripted-review, scripted-overlord and scripted-decompose (membership, not equality);
- GET /api/v0/models returns 200 and every entry has state "loaded";
- LMStudioProvider().reachable(base_url) returns (True, "") and loaded_models(base_url) contains "scripted-dispatch" (drive the real provider against the real server - integration, no mocks);
- cursor_state() is identical before and after both GETs;
- negative: GET /v1/unknown still returns 404; GET /v1/chat/completions still returns 405; POST /v1/models returns 404.

SUCCESS: new tests pass; full suite and `ruff check .` green. No production file changes. Do not modify any existing test.

stories.summary: Start and supervise the scheduler daemon from the image entrypoint
stories.description: Only the smoke compose shim starts the scheduler, nothing restarts or notices it if it dies, and deploy/README.md says the image starts it.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master c57a596 - stand-in of SG-01..SG-06: 1 conflict for this story, tests/smoke/test_deploy_contract.py::test_compose_entrypoint_defers_shell_expansion_to_the_container, pre-authorized below.

PROBLEM: deploy/entrypoint.sh starts the dashboard and the MCP transport and watches both, but never starts the scheduler daemon. Only deploy/compose.yaml's `pipeline` service shim does (`python -m pipeline.scheduler_daemon &`), unsupervised. deploy/README.md ("What the image is not") already claims the ENTRYPOINT starts the daemon and that PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON=0 turns it off. Make the code match the doc.

FIX:
- deploy/entrypoint.sh: default `PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON="${PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON:-1}"`. When it is `1`, start `python -m pipeline.scheduler_daemon &` (log a line first, like the other two), record its pid, include it in `shutdown()`'s kill list and in the final kill/wait, and add a third check to the supervision loop so the container exits non-zero with `log "scheduler daemon exited"` when the daemon dies - the same shape as the dashboard and MCP checks. When it is `0`, start nothing and skip that check. Any other value: `die "PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON must be 0 or 1"` (fail closed, before starting anything).
- deploy/compose.yaml: delete the shim's `if [ "$${PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON:-0}" = "1" ]; then ... fi` block (the echo and the `python -m pipeline.scheduler_daemon &`); keep `PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON: "1"` in the service environment and keep `exec /app/deploy/entrypoint.sh` as the last line. Update the shim's comment and deploy/README.md's "How the pipeline container is wired" list (step 3 no longer starts the daemon; the image entrypoint does) and the `## Required environment` table (add PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON, default `1`).

AUTHORIZED EDIT to an existing test (exactly this, nothing else; commit-body justification: "the compose shim no longer reads PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON; the image entrypoint does"):
- tests/smoke/test_deploy_contract.py, in test_compose_entrypoint_defers_shell_expansion_to_the_container, delete the one tuple element line `        "$${PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON:-0}",` from the first (escaped) tuple. Leave the unescaped tuple's `'"${PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON:-0}"',` entry in place (it still guards against reintroducing an unescaped reference).
Paired replacement assertions so the story cannot pass as a no-op (new file tests/smoke/test_entrypoint_scheduler.py, read files as text and run the script with stub binaries on PATH where useful):
- deploy/compose.yaml no longer contains `pipeline.scheduler_daemon`;
- deploy/entrypoint.sh starts `pipeline.scheduler_daemon` and its supervision loop names the daemon (string `scheduler daemon exited`);
- run entrypoint.sh under bash with a fake `python` on PATH whose `-m pipeline.scheduler_daemon` invocation exits 3 after 1 second while the other two sleep: the script exits non-zero and stderr contains `scheduler daemon exited` (set PLAN_DIR/WORKTREE_ROOT to tmp dirs and PIPELINE_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=shared to skip the secret check);
- PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON=0 with the same fakes: the fake python is never invoked with `pipeline.scheduler_daemon` (record argv to a file);
- negative: PIPELINE_SCHEDULER_DAEMON=yes exits non-zero with `must be 0 or 1` before any process starts.

SUCCESS: new tests pass; the edited test passes; full suite and `ruff check .` green.

stories.summary: Name the exception class when an event handler fails
stories.description: A failing event handler logs only the event type, so a dead-lettered agent_done needed a manual reproduction to find its cause.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master c57a596 - stand-in of SG-01..SG-06: 0 conflicts for this story.

PROBLEM (verified live 2026-10-29): when wake_handler raised `RuntimeError` (git commit failed), the container log had only `Event handler failed for event type agent_done` and `dead-lettering a agent_done event: handler wake_handler failed`. The cause took a hand reproduction to find. The log must carry the exception CLASS NAME - never the exception message, the payload or a traceback, because the message can carry event contents (the existing comments say so; keep that rule).

FIX - three sites, each logs `type(exc).__name__` as a structured field `error_type` (extra={"error_type": ...}) AND appends it to the message (`... for event type %s (%s)`), keeping level ERROR:
1. pipeline/events_nats.py `_dispatch`: `except Exception:` -> `except Exception as exc:`.
2. pipeline/event_wiring.py, the `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001` around `handler(event)` in the dispatching JSONL bus's publish.
3. pipeline/events_nats_consumer.py: the function that runs handlers returns only the failing handler's name (`return _handler_name(handler)` inside `except Exception:`). Make the dead-letter / redelivery log line that consumes that result also name the exception class: change the helper to return the handler name and the class name (a tuple, or a small NamedTuple) and update its one caller's log line. Keep `None` for 'all handlers returned'.
Keep the existing comments' intent (no payload, no exception text) and update them to say the class name is logged.

TESTS (write first, new file tests/unit/test_event_handler_failure_logging.py; use caplog and in-process fakes, the existing nats tests' _FakeJetStream pattern for the consumer):
- for each of the three sites, a handler raising `RuntimeError("secret-payload-text")` produces an ERROR record whose message contains `RuntimeError` and whose `error_type` attribute is `RuntimeError`;
- negative, each site: the record's message and every attribute value do NOT contain `secret-payload-text`;
- a handler that returns normally produces no ERROR record;
- two handlers where the first raises: the second still runs (existing guarantee, keep it).

SUCCESS: new tests pass; full suite and `ruff check .` green. Do not modify any existing test.
